name: You Had to Be There (Jodie Harsh)
heard: memoir / my book / the book / you had to be there / your book
context: Jodie's memoir of a decade in 2000s London nightlife, one club per chapter, out on 25 September 2025; it ends with a list of friends the scene lost

name: London
context: Where the 15-year-old from a small town 90 minutes away by train had to be - to be around people like her

name: Jodie Harsh
context: Guest: DJ, producer and London club host, described on the show as Britain's busiest drag queen; her memoir You Had to Be There follows her 2000s London club years

name: New York
context: Jodie's sister city for London: she came for two weeks as a young writer, met Amanda Lepore and took a bit of its club flavour home

name: Nag Nag Nag
heard: nag nag nag / Nag Nag Nag / Nygmatic
context: The Wednesday night at The Ghetto that was London's hub of electroclash around 2003-04 - and where people started being freaks again, as James reads it in the book

name: Jodie's sobriety
context: Jodie says she woke up one day with the worst hangover of her life and stopped - 15 years ago now; she DJs from the booth, last in and first out

name: DJ Fat Tony
context: Jodie says he has helped so many people get sober and has been there every step of her way; it was his night at the Hippodrome when the Pop Tarts played

name: Heaven (London)
context: Her weekly hangout after G-A-Y - mainstream gay, as James puts it - with loads of drag and the Wednesday night party in the powder room

name: Booby Tuesday
context: Nag Nag Nag star in a painted white body stocking - very Leigh Bowery, Jodie says - whose make-up melted down her face by morning

name: Booby Tuesday's painted body stocking
context: A white all-in-one body stocking with drag make-up painted on top, sweating through and smearing by 7am; next to her, Miss K in neon-highlighter make-up

name: Amanda Lepore
context: Jodie interviewed her at Hotel 17 - a poster girl on her wall, shot by LaChapelle - and Amanda took her out to New York club nights

name: Fenton Bailey
context: Co-host; he and Randy are the reason, as James tells it, that this episode came about once Jodie said she was writing a book

name: Too 2 Much (Raymond Revuebar)
heard: 2.2 / Raymond / too much / too too much
context: The old Raymond Revuebar strip club in Soho, by then Too 2 Much: Jodie's own Friday night there, Circus, began with her 21st birthday party

name: James St. James
context: Host; he had just finished Jodie's book and steers the talk club by club

name: Philip Sallon
context: James remembers him turning his back that night; Jodie says she gets the same cool greeting from him to this day

name: Kim Jones
context: Then just one of the designers going to Nag Nag Nag every Wednesday; he dressed Jodie up and lent her vintage Westwood

name: Happy Valley (New York)
heard: Happy valley / Happy, valiant / happy, valiant
context: A New York night Amanda took Jodie to, with a leopard carpet Jodie thinks Jeremy Scott designed

name: RuPaul
context: Jodie believes Ru did a G-A-Y show too

name: G-A-Y
context: Her first ever night out, aged 15 in 2001, on a terrible fake ID: every Saturday at the Astoria a huge pop act performed

name: Pet Shop Boys
heard: pack shop / pet shop / pets up
context: In the roped-off VIP that night; James was too shy to talk to them then but found them the chattiest at a dinner years later

name: Alexander McQueen
context: Jodie saw him at Nag Nag Nag and met him at Drama

name: The Face
context: Relaunched while Jodie was a student interning at magazines - she helped out in the fashion cupboard and borrowed from it

name: Puking over the crowd
context: Food poisoning from the Mr Wu buffet hit mid-set: Jodie threw up from the stage over about a hundred people - and stayed till the end of her shift

name: Leigh Bowery
heard: Lee Barry / Lee Lee Barry / Leigh
context: Booby Tuesday's look recalled him; the hosts joke about his own stage act after Jodie's puking story - he was before her time, she reminds them

name: The melted wig
context: A diva with a can of hairspray and a lighter melted one side of Jodie's wig - the side, by luck, where she wore her hair; her only fight, she says

name: Room Service
context: Jodie's gay party from 2010, started just after she got sober and needed the rent: up-and-coming DJs like Honey Dijon, a tops-off crowd, inspired by New York

name: Tasty Tim
context: James loves him to the end of time - part of the old Boy George and Marilyn crowd - and asks Jodie to help get Tasty Tim on the show; Tasty Tim was on the bill at Fat Tony's Hippodrome night

name: Circus (London club night)
context: Her Friday night at Too 2 Much that became the hot spot fast: paparazzi camped outside and the papers writing about it every day

name: Boombox
context: Sunday night in East London, mid-2000s, free and over by 1am: a fashion crowd with Judy Blame, Pam Hogg, Gareth Pugh, Christopher Bailey and Kim Jones, and designers on the decks

name: Camden
context: Where Jodie moved - for a while the centre of the world, very rock and roll

name: Harriet (literary agent)
context: The literary agent at CAA who took Jodie to lunch and talked her into writing one chapter

name: Randy Barbato
context: Co-host; he remembers the Pop Tarts playing Fat Tony's night at the Hippodrome, with Fenton's father in the audience

name: Trade at Turnmills
context: Jodie went to a couple of Trades - the after-hours that ran all the way into Sunday afternoon

name: Harry Potter
context: James likens British schools to something out of a dark Harry Potter

name: Section 28
context: Only just repealed when Jodie was at school: the law that stopped schools talking about being gay

name: Instagram
context: James: today you can find that sense of belonging on Instagram; Fat Tony posts pictures there

name: Macaulay Culkin
context: Also in the VIP at the Party Monster premiere party - he played Michael Alig in the film

name: Pete Burns
context: A Nag Nag Nag regular, and at the Party Monster premiere party where James met him

name: Bianca Jagger
context: James thinks she was at the premiere party too

name: Electroclash
context: The 2003-04 sound Nag Nag Nag was the London home of

name: Boy George
context: Would come and DJ at Nag Nag Nag sometimes, Jodie says; James places Tasty Tim in his old crowd

name: Nag Nag Nag dress-up
context: Drag with flower pots on her head, pieces borrowed (or nicked) from the fashion cupboard at The Face, vintage shop finds and Kim Jones's priceless vintage Westwood, rolled around on the floor
fashion: Flower pots on the head, borrowed couture, vintage Westwood

name: Ministry of Sound
context: Where, in her second year at university, she started getting paid: go-go dancing on stage in drag for 65 to 100 pounds a night and hanging out behind the DJ booth

name: Soho, London
context: Home of Mr Wu, the Raymond Revuebar and Too 2 Much

name: The Cross (King's Cross)
context: Beautiful club built under railway arches in King's Cross - London's answer to the Tunnel, as the hosts see it; now a Tom Dixon shop

name: Tunnel
context: The hosts compare The Cross to New York's Tunnel - also built under arches

name: Skin (Skunk Anansie)
context: One of the stars Jodie met at Drama

name: Hotel 17
context: Where Jodie sat in Amanda Lepore's room for the interview

name: Amy Winehouse
context: Jodie's best friend in the Camden years - they lived close and were always at each other's houses; she remembers her as very sweet and caring

name: Amy's beehive and Jodie's waterfall
context: James pictures the two falling out of limos together, her beehive next to Jodie's waterfall of hair; Jodie keeps a Polaroid Amy took in a shoebox

name: YouTube
context: What Jodie watches at home in bed while the dancing goes on

name: Shannon – 'Let the Music Play'
context: The hosts' suggestion for that unifying moment

name: Eight-way auction for You Had to Be There
context: Her literary agent sent the proposal round and eight publishers bid; Jodie went to every pitch meeting in drag

name: The Fabulous Pop Tarts
context: Fenton and Randy's band played Fat Tony's night at the Hippodrome, with Tasty Tim on the bill; Fenton's father painted a picture of them

name: World of Wonder
context: Fenton and Randy's company, as James says in the intro

name: RuPaul's Drag Race UK
context: James's intro: Jodie has been on it twice

name: London Astoria
context: The venue G-A-Y filled every Saturday - long gone, now a train station; Nag Nag Nag's little club sat right behind it

name: Kylie Minogue
context: One of the pop stars Jodie remembers performing at G-A-Y

name: Steps
context: Another of the G-A-Y Saturday acts Jodie remembers

name: S Club 7
context: Another of the G-A-Y Saturday acts Jodie remembers

name: Belinda Carlisle
context: Another of the G-A-Y Saturday acts Jodie remembers

name: The Copa (Fort Lauderdale)
context: James did the same at 15: out of the window, down the highway on his bike, in with a fake ID

name: Fort Lauderdale
context: Where James snuck into the Copa at 15

name: Margaret Thatcher
context: James reminds everyone that Section 28 was brought in under her government

name: Disco Bloodbath / Party Monster (James St. James)
context: James told his mother she was welcome to read it, but he wasn't discussing it with her

name: Blitz Club
context: James's yardstick: Nag Nag Nag came about 20 years after the Blitz Kids

name: Kinky Gerlinky
context: The other London dress-up night James measures Nag Nag Nag against

name: Party Monster premiere party (London)
context: Jodie went to the Party Monster premiere party around the Nag Nag Nag years, on a night off; a picture of her with James has just turned up

name: Party Monster (2003)
context: Fenton and Randy's film - its premiere party is where Jodie first crossed paths with James

name: Steve Strange
context: James met him at the Party Monster premiere party

name: The Ghetto (London)
context: Small club for two or three hundred behind the Astoria: low ceiling, walls painted red, its own weather system of dripping condensation and a crackly sound system

name: Scissor Sisters
context: Jodie remembers them doing a performance at Nag Nag Nag

name: John Galliano
context: Another Nag Nag Nag face Jodie remembers

name: Vivienne Westwood
context: The priceless vintage pieces Kim lent Jodie, which she rolled around the Nag Nag Nag floor in

name: Kingsley
context: One of Jodie's best friends, all through the book; the scene lost him last year

name: Drama

name: King's Cross
context: Where The Cross was, under the railway arches

name: Tom Dixon

name: Marilyn

context: One of the Boombox fashion crowd James names

context: One of the Boombox fashion crowd James names

context: One of the Boombox fashion crowd James names

name: East London

name: Hedi Slimane
